content:
jonathan: Ran an nsys + perfetto spotcheck on the dedicated pool after the kernel-affinity change. Quick summary: queue-time spikes line up with the end of the continuous batch window (around 12–16ms), kernel chooser oscillates between cutlass/cuBLAS, and a KV-cache miss wave coincides. Posting the short nsys capture and a tiny trace excerpt.

jonathan: nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=all --capture-range=nvtx -t 10 
# then extract timeline in perfetto
```

kevin: can you paste the perfetto slice (top-down)? suspect host->GPU memcpy or stream serialization at the end of the window. :thinking:

jonathan: perfetto raw slice (abbrev):
```
time(ms)  event
  0-4    GPU compute active (kernel A)
  4-13   queue tail accumulation (many small launches)
 13-16   sudden kernel switch + KV-cache miss sweep (50% higher misses)
 16-20   longer host-side memcpy bursts
```

maria: I ran a microbench toggling the kernel chooser heuristic (affinity ON vs OFF). Results (single node, seq8/seq512):
- seq8 p95: affinity ON -> +12% latency
- seq512 throughput: affinity ON -> +9% throughput
So affinity helps long sequences but hurts short interactive ones.

alex: interesting. try two quick controls: cut the continuous_batch_window_ms from 16 -> 10, and lower kv_cache_prefetch_frac to 0.3. also compare `continuous` vs `adaptive` batching mode. config snippet:
```yaml
serving: 
  batching:
    mode: adaptive # vs continuous
    continuous_window_ms: 10
  kv_cache:
    prefetch_fraction: 0.3
```

jonathan: ran the adaptive vs continuous A/B for 30s steady load (seq8 dominant). TL;DR: adaptive reduced p99 by ~14% and smoothed kernel selection variance. continuous had higher tail due to the end-of-window tailspike.

perf-bot: Regression detector: +14% p99 on model "redwood-mini-v2" on main vs release/236. Links: <https://ci/reports/246|report>

sara: ok actionable triage plan: (1) reproduce with nsys on a dedicated machine and include host perf counters (context-switches, syscalls), (2) perfetto flame + GPU slices for both adaptive/continuous modes, (3) experiment with max batch wait cap (try 8ms) to prevent long tail formation, (4) collect KV-cache hitmap across the run and compare. I'll file a GH issue with the checklist.

alex: ack. I'll wire up a quick flag `--max-batch-wait-ms=8` and run against the same load.

kevin: also check host-side scheduler: I saw syscalls bunch at ~15ms on the node that had the worst tail. might be preemption/IRQ related.

maria: noted. i'll collate the microbench csvs and KV hit heatmaps.

jonathan: thanks — i'll attach the full nsys capture and the perfetto trace to the GH issue once it's up. short-term mitigation: flip the default to `adaptive` for small-instance SKU until we understand kernel-affinity effects on short sequences. :thumbsup:
